cards.explanation: The answer is a vegetable garden. Ahab, king of Samaria, says, “Give me your vineyard to use as a vegetable garden, since it is next to my palace.” A whole palace, and he's still eyeing the lot next door. It's like me owning a bakery and sizing up the empty space next to it for more counter room.

The answer is silver. Ahab gives Naboth two choices: a better vineyard in its place, or if Naboth prefers, the vineyard's value in silver. Naboth is the vineyard's owner, and he answers, “The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.” Silver, a better vineyard, take your pick, and the man still says no. A king standing at your door with a blank check, and you just say no! I can't even say no to a second helping of my own dough.

The answer is that it's the inheritance of his fathers. Naboth says, “The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.” (1 Kings 21:3) He doesn't haggle or ask for time to think. Me, I might have asked what the better vineyard looked like, friends, so Naboth is a stronger man than I am.
The answer is eat. Ahab lies down on his bed, turns his face away and refuses to eat. I'd wave a cookie under his nose, but I think this one needed more than that.

The answer is False. Naboth told Ahab that the vineyard was “…the inheritance of my fathers.” (1 Kings 21:3). But when Ahab tells Jezebel, he only reports Naboth saying, “I will not give you my vineyard!” That part about his fathers never makes it into the retelling.

The answer is that she will get him Naboth's vineyard. Jezebel, Ahab's wife, tells him, “…I will get you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.” Ahab is lying there with his face turned away, and she walks in and promises him a whole vineyard. That's a lot of confidence for one visit, friends.

The answer is True. Jezebel writes the letters in Ahab's name, seals them with his seal, and sends them to the elders and nobles who lived with Naboth in his city. Jezebel wrote them, but they carry Ahab's name and Ahab's seal. The leaders of Naboth's city got letters that looked like they came from the king.

The word is scoundrels. Jezebel's letters say to “…seat two scoundrels opposite him…” (1 Kings 21:10). It's right there in the instructions, plain as can be. Those two men are sitting across from Naboth for a reason, friends.

The answer is cursing both God and the king. Jezebel's letters say the two men are to testify, “You have cursed both God and the king!” (1 Kings 21:10) Her plan has them say it in front of everyone. It's a heavy charge, friends.

The answer is True. The elders and nobles of Naboth's city “…did as Jezebel had instructed in the letters she had written to them.” (1 Kings 21:11) They followed the letters, step by step. This is a heavy part of the story, friends.

The answer is that she tells him to go take possession of the vineyard. Jezebel, Ahab's wife, tells him, “Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite…” Naboth, the vineyard's owner, is gone, and she points her husband straight at the land. I think it's a hard thing to read, friends.

The answer is True. The text says Ahab “…got up and went down to take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.” This is the same king who lay on his bed with his face turned away (1 Kings 21:4). He's moving now. I think this part of the story hurts, friends.

The answer is to go down and meet King Ahab. The LORD tells Elijah the Tishbite, God's prophet, “Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria.” He also tells Elijah where to find him: in Naboth's vineyard, where Ahab has gone to take possession of it. So Elijah's errand is a face-to-face meeting.

The answer is that dogs will lick up Ahab's blood where they licked Naboth's. The LORD says, “In the place where the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth, there also the dogs will lick up your blood…” He names the place where the dogs licked up Naboth's blood, and says Ahab's blood will be licked up there too. It's a heavy word, friends.

The answer is True. Ahab says to Elijah, “So you have found me out, my enemy.” Elijah replies, “I have found you out because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the LORD.” Elijah gives the reason straight.

The answer is that Ahab provoked His anger and caused Israel to sin. The LORD says, “…because you have provoked My anger and caused Israel to sin.” (1 Kings 21:22) Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah are the two houses He compares Ahab's to. The LORD gives His reason, friends, and it's about Ahab's own actions.

The answer is Jezreel. The LORD says, “The dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.” Jezebel is Ahab's wife, and the LORD speaks about her too. It's the same city where Naboth's vineyard sits. This is a heavy word, friends.

The answer is sackcloth. The text says Ahab “…tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and fasted.” Ahab heard every word from Elijah, and then he acted. This is the same king who called Elijah his enemy earlier in this passage.

The answer is False. The LORD does not say Ahab hasn't humbled himself. He says to Elijah, “Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before Me?” He goes on, “Because he has humbled himself before Me, I will not bring the calamity during his days…” So the LORD Himself says Ahab humbled himself.

The answer is that the calamity will come on his house in his son's days. The LORD says, “…I will not bring the calamity during his days, but I will bring it upon his house in the days of his son.” So Ahab's humbling changes when it comes, and the word about his house stays. It's a serious word, friends, and it's worth reading slowly.
